title: Sharing equally from a line plot

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four identical beakers. Half a liter, three fourths, one liter, and one and three fourths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The line plot records those amounts. Each step is one fourth of a liter. Each *x* stands for one beaker.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Share all the water equally. How many liters in each beaker?

do.text: Share all the water equally. How many liters in each beaker?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The fullest one can give some to the others.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Follow the four marks back to their beakers.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Move half a liter from the fullest beaker into the first one. One falls as the other rises.

do.text: The total water stays the same.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Then move one fourth of a liter into the second beaker.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: All four water levels match. One liter each!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The arithmetic tells the same story. Add all four starting amounts.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: In fourths, that is two plus three plus four plus seven fourths. Sixteen fourths makes four liters altogether.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four liters shared among four beakers: one liter each.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This equal share is called the mean: the total divided by how many measurements there are.

do.meaning: The total divided by the number of measurements.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Share all the water equally again. Each step is one eighth of a liter. Some amounts occur twice.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: There are four different amounts. Do I add those four?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That would leave out two beakers. Count every *x*, including both marks at one eighth, and both at one half.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One, two, three, four, five, six. Six beakers!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One eighth, one eighth, three eighths. One half, one half, five eighths. Each mark contributes its own water.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here are the six beakers. Rename each half as four eighths, so we can count equal sized parts.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One plus one plus three plus four plus four plus five makes eighteen eighths in all.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Sixteen eighths is two whole liters, with two eighths left. So the total is two and one fourth liters.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: And I divide by six beakers, not four different amounts.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Eighteen eighths shared six ways gives three eighths to each. Watch the water reach that level.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The two half liter beakers each give one eighth to the second beaker.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Six equal shares. Three eighths of a liter in every beaker.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Check the answer against the original measurements. The least was one eighth. The greatest was five eighths.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three eighths is between them.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The equal share lies from the least to the greatest amount. We only moved water; we did not add or remove any.

do.text: The total amount stays the same.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Champ, these marks show five ribbon lengths. Join all the ribbon. Cut five equal pieces. How many feet per piece?

do.text: Join the ribbon; cut 5 equal pieces.
Join all the ribbon. Cut 5 equal pieces. How many feet per piece?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I count five marks. The half foot length appears twice, so I add it twice.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One fourth and three fourths make one foot. The two halves make another foot. Plus the whole foot: three feet altogether.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Here are the lengths. When I join them, the total stays three feet.

do.text: Join the lengths without changing them.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Five equal pieces means three divided by five. Each piece is three fifths of a foot.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Separate the five equal shares. Five copies of three fifths use all three feet.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to our six beakers: the same total water, shared equally.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add every *x*. Divide by how many *x* marks. That is the amount each would have if all were made equal.

do.text: Add one amount for every X.
Divide by the number of Xs.
